items.title: Somali journalist Bashir Mohamed Abdullahi dies after being shot during Baidoa clashes
items.description: MOGADISHU, Somalia 7 September 2026 – The Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) expresses its deepest condolences over the death of journalist Bashir Mohamed Abdullahi, also known as Bashir Moalin, a reporter with the local Arlaadi Media Network, who succumbed to gunshot injuries sustained during armed clashes in Baidoa on Thursday, 3 September 2026. He becomes the second journalist killed in Somalia this year. Early on Monday, 7 September 2026, Bashir, 28, died from critical injuries he sustained while seeking shelter during armed clashes in Baidoa, Southwest State, his family told SJS. Accordin
items.titleIt: Somali journalist Bashir Mohamed Abdullahi dies after being shot during Baidoa clashes

items.title: Boy, 6, in coma after pool accident in Egypt being flown back to Italy - Tajani
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, SEP 3 - A six-year-old boy who has been in a coma in an Egyptian hospital since an August 3 accident at a swimming pool at Sharm El Sheikh is currently being flown back to Italy, Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said on a visit to Cairo Thursday. The boy, Younes Majidi, who suffered a cardiac arrest and has been in critical condition since nearly drowning at the Red Sea resort, will be admitted for treatment at the Regina Margherita Children's Hospital in Turin, said Tajani, who is also deputy premier. items.description: [Dabanga] Nyala -- The Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have released four female journalists and a lawyer in Nyala, the capital of South Darfur, after holding them for varying periods of time. Sources tell Radio Dabanga that the journalists, Dr Manahil Mustafa, Ishraqa Abdelrahman, Mawahib Ibrahim, and Zahra Mohamed El Hassan, were released alongside the lawyer, Magda Hassan Ali, after about six months in detention.
